stemMd: A heat engine absorbs 900 J from a hot reservoir and rejects 600 J to a cold reservoir in each cycle. What is its efficiency?
explanationMd: Net work per cycle is 900 − 600 = 300 J. Efficiency is useful work divided by heat absorbed, 300/900 = 1/3. The rejected heat is necessary to include in the energy balance.

distractorRationale.c: This is the fraction rejected as heat, not converted to work.
distractorRationale.e: An efficiency above one would violate energy conservation here.
distractorRationale.b: This divides work by rejected heat rather than absorbed heat.
distractorRationale.d: The engine rejects a substantial part of the input heat.
